rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 128.9, up from 49.6): no run finished. The oval reached progress 0.61, the s-bend 0.26 and the slalom 0.10, and every run ended off_track with max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m against the 0.06 m limit. Line-loss events fell from 1-2 to 1.0-1.9 per run, so the sensor_size and kd changes helped, but the robot still loses the tape. The body width cannot widen the limit: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 m for any allowed width. The robot has to stay on the line. Steering oscillation rose to 0.28 on the oval with kd 0.3, which is still low, so kd 0.3 is not too much. The Evaluator's conditional rule applies: line loss persists at 1 or more events per run with sensor_size 0.012, so I raise sensor_size to the largest allowed value, 0.016 m. The 16 mm footprint covers the tape edge fully and should keep the signal non-zero when the robot drifts. I change only geometry.sensor_size and leave the controller unchanged (base_speed 1.3, kp 2.0, kd 0.3, ki 0.05, weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], last_direction), so the effect of the footprint can be isolated. Expected result: line_loss_events near 0 to 1 per run, max_error below about 0.055 m, and higher progress on all three tracks. Hypotheses and measurements for next: (1) if line loss drops but max_error still reaches 0.06 on sharp bends, kp is too low for the bend curvature, so raise kp in steps of about 0.5 next; (2) if the robot stays on the line with completion_time above 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.2, as the Evaluator advised; (3) watch steering_oscillation to make sure kd 0.3 stays well-damped. I need per-track max_error, line_loss_events, progress, completion_time and steering_oscillation to decide the next step.
